sides.text: A bank posts signs warning that all branches are monitored by cameras. Which control type does this mainly represent?
D. Deterrent

more.text: Signs discourage by perception. They don't physically stop anyone (preventive) or repair damage (corrective).

sides.text: After a ransomware attack, an organization restores its files from clean backups. Which control type is this?
B. Corrective

more.text: Restoring repairs the damage after the event, which makes it corrective.

sides.text: A legacy server can't be patched, so the team isolates it on a segmented VLAN with strict firewall rules. Which control type is this?
A. Compensating

more.text: Isolation stands in for the patch that couldn't be applied, so it's a compensating control.

sides.text: Which control category includes risk assessments and security policies written by senior leaders?
D. Managerial

more.text: Managerial controls govern and oversee risk. Technical controls are enforced by systems; operational ones are carried out by people.

sides.text: An employee denies sending a contract that carries their digital signature. Which concept prevents this denial?
C. Non-repudiation

more.text: The signature, made with the signer's private key, proves they sent it. That is non-repudiation.

sides.text: A user logs in with a password and then confirms a code from a hardware token. Which factors are used?
options: Something you have and somewhere you are
Something you know and something you have
Something you know and something you are

sides.text: B. Something you know and something you have

more.text: A password is knowledge and a token is possession. Two different categories makes it MFA.

sides.text: A log shows which administrator changed a firewall rule and when. Which part of AAA provides this?
D. Accounting

more.text: Accounting records what users do. Authentication proves identity and authorization grants permissions.

sides.text: In a zero trust architecture, which component evaluates policy and context and decides whether to grant access?
A. Policy engine

more.text: The policy engine decides. The policy enforcement point carries out that decision on the data plane.

sides.text: Which zero trust plane contains the policy enforcement point?
C. Data plane

more.text: The data plane enforces decisions. The control plane holds the policy engine and policy administrator.

sides.text: A data center entrance has two interlocking doors that admit one verified person at a time. Which control is this?
C. Access control vestibule

more.text: An access control vestibule (a mantrap) stops tailgating by admitting one person at a time.

sides.text: A team places a bait file named Executive_Salaries.xlsx on a server that alerts when opened. Which technology is this?
A. Honeyfile

more.text: A bait file is a honeyfile. A honeytoken is fake data or credentials, and a honeypot is a decoy system.

sides.text: A change to a production database is approved, but there is no plan to undo it if it fails. Which element is missing?
C. Backout plan

more.text: A backout plan defines how to restore the previous state if the change fails.

sides.text: A firm schedules network changes for Sunday at 2 a.m. to reduce business impact. What is this called?
D. Maintenance window

more.text: A maintenance window is an agreed time for changes with minimal business impact.

sides.text: Which statement best describes a cryptographic hash?
options: A way to hide data inside images
A reversible function that encrypts data with a key
A one-way function that produces a fixed-length digest

sides.text: D. A one-way function that produces a fixed-length digest

more.text: Hashes can't be reversed and output a fixed length. They check integrity; they aren't encryption.

sides.text: Why is salting used when storing password hashes?
options: It makes identical passwords produce different hashes and defeats rainbow tables

sides.text: B. It makes identical passwords produce different hashes and defeats rainbow tables

more.text: A unique salt per password means precomputed tables are useless and duplicate passwords don't match.

sides.text: Which tamper-resistant device is used to generate and store keys for servers and certificate authorities?
D. HSM

more.text: An HSM is dedicated hardware for key protection. A TPM is a chip on a single device's motherboard.

sides.text: A certificate has been revoked and clients should check one certificate's status in real time. Which protocol is used?
B. OCSP

more.text: OCSP queries a responder for one certificate's status. A CRL is a downloaded list.

sides.text: A web admin needs one certificate to cover mail.example.com and shop.example.com. Which type fits best?
B. Wildcard

more.text: A wildcard certificate (*.example.com) covers all subdomains of a domain.

sides.text: A payment processor replaces stored card numbers with random values and keeps the originals in a vault. Which technique is this?
D. Tokenization

more.text: Tokenization swaps data for tokens with the real value held in a vault. Masking only hides part of a displayed value.

sides.text: Which provides integrity, authentication, and non-repudiation but not confidentiality?
D. Digital signature

more.text: A signature proves origin and unaltered content. It doesn't hide the message.

sides.text: Two parties who have never met must agree on a shared key over an untrusted network. Which approach is used?
C. Key exchange such as Diffie-Hellman

more.text: Key exchange derives a shared secret without sending it. Hashing and salting don't establish keys.

sides.text: A laptop is stolen. Which control best keeps the data on its drive unreadable?
D. Full-disk encryption

more.text: Full-disk encryption protects data at rest on a lost device.

sides.text: A gap analysis shows a company meets 70% of a framework's controls. What does this help with?
options: Prioritizing improvements toward the target standard

sides.text: C. Prioritizing improvements toward the target standard

more.text: Gap analysis compares the current state with a target and shows what must change.

sides.text: A software update requires restarting a critical service. What should the change process include?
options: Scheduling the restart in a maintenance window with stakeholder notice

sides.text: A. Scheduling the restart in a maintenance window with stakeholder notice

more.text: Planning restarts and downtime is a technical implication of change management.

sides.text: Which statement best describes least privilege?
options: Granting only the access needed to do a job

sides.text: C. Granting only the access needed to do a job

more.text: Least privilege limits the damage from mistakes and compromise.
